([[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]]) | college = [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] (2019–2021) | highlights = * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Sixth Man of the Year (2021) | medal_templates = }} '''Kai Martinez Jones''' (born January 19, 2001) is a Bahamian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==Early life== Born in [[Nassau, Bahamas]], Jones moved to the United States when he was 11 years old. Before high school, he returned to his home country hoping to pursue a career as a [[long jump|long jumper]]. At age 15, Jones played organized basketball for his first time, being drawn to the sport after having a growth spurt.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Kai Jones shows well at Global Academy, as interest picks up |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Kai-Jones-shows-well-at-Global-Academy-as-college-interest-picks-up-118810166/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=June 5, 2018}} ==High school career== In the summer of 2017, Jones took part in a [[Basketball Without Borders]] Americas camp held by the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) in Nassau.{{cite web |title=BWB Americas come to an end in The Bahamas |url=https://thenassauguardian.com/2017/07/11/bwb-americas-come-to-an-end-in-the-bahamas/ |website=[[The Nassau Guardian]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=July 11, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Scouting the most interesting draft prospects at the NBA Global Camp |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23651773/2018-nba-draft-scouting-international-prospects-new-global-camp |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=June 7, 2018}} That year, he worked out with and took advice from top high school recruit [[Deandre Ayton]] in their hometown of Nassau. As a result, Jones was inspired to play basketball in the United States.{{cite web |last1=McMullen |first1=Ryan |title=Texas lands Bahamian big man Kai Jones, who worked out with Deandre Ayton |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2018/10/15/kai-jones-to-texas/ |publisher=Zagsblog |accessdate=September 14, 2019 |date=October 15, 2018}} For the 2017–18 season, he enrolled at [[Orlando Christian Prep]] in [[Orlando, Florida]], as a high school senior. He was teammates with five-star recruits [[Nassir Little]] and C. J. Walker and helped win the [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSAA) Class 3A state championship.{{cite web |last1=Perper |first1=Jake |title=2019 F Kai Jones talks OCP state title, recruitment and more |url=https://www.prephoops.com/2018/06/2019-f-kai-jones-talks-ocp-state-title-recruitment-and-more/ |publisher=Prep Hoops |accessdate=September 14, 2019 |date=June 5, 2018}}{{cite web |last1=Kemp |first1=Bill |title=Canterbury falls in Class 3A state championship game |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2018/03/06/boys-basketball-canterbury-falls-class-3-championship-game/399491002/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |accessdate=September 14, 2019 |date=March 7, 2018}} In high school, Jones woke up at 4:45 a.m. every day to train and played basketball after school.{{cite web |last1=Dorsett |first1=Renaldo |title=Kai Jones Commits To The University Of Texas Longhorns |url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2018/oct/16/kai-jones-commits-university-texas-longhorns/ |website=The Tribune |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=October 16, 2018}} At the same time, he saw academic success, graduating with a 4.2 [[Grading in education|grade point average]] and [[Latin honors|summa cum laude]] honors. In the summer of 2018, Jones attended the NBA Global Camp in [[Treviso]], Italy. Following his senior year, he played a [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate]] season at [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]].{{cite web |last1=Snow |first1=Brian |title=Kai Jones shows major potential and is ready to make impact |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Top-60-prospect-Kai-Jones-is-ready-to-make-an-impact-for-Shaka-Smart-at-Texas-127221347/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=January 2, 2019}} On February 4, 2019, Jones was named to the National Prep Invitational all-tournament team.{{cite web |last1=Dorsett |first1=Renaldo |title=Jones Named In Tournament Team |url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2019/feb/06/jones-named-tournament-team/ |website=The Tribune |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=February 6, 2019}} In March, he helped Brewster Academy win the USA National Prep Championship.{{cite web |last1=French |first1=Simba |title=Jones, Brewster Academy win National Prep Championships |url=https://thenassauguardian.com/2019/03/12/jones-brewster-academy-win-national-prep-championships/ |website=[[The Nassau Guardian]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== On October 15, 2018, Jones committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]]. He chose to join the Longhorns over offers from several other [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web |last1=Holland |first1=EJ |title=Four-star big man Kai Jones commits to Texas |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2018/10/16/four-star-big-man-kai-jones-commits-to-texas/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=October 15, 2018}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Kai Jones | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Nassau, Bahamas]] | highschool = [[Brewster Academy]] (NH) | feet = 6 | inches = 10 | weight = 205 | 40 = | commitdate = October 15, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 88 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Texas 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Texas Longhorns Recruiting Class | rivals school = texas | scout s = | espn schoolid = 251 | 247 overall = 49 | rivals overall = 59 | espn overall = 53 | accessdate = September 15, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Coach [[Shaka Smart]] said that Jones had the best work ethic of any big man he coached. Despite this, Jones struggled to get playing time early in his freshman season. He gradually saw more playing time as the season progressed, finishing with eight points on 4–5 shooting from the field in just 10 minutes of the Longhorns’ 73–71 win over [[McNeese State Cowboys men's basketball|McNeese State]] on November 30.{{cite news |last1=Dorsett |first1=Renaldo |title=Kai Jones Wants More Playing Time With Texas Longhorns |url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2019/dec/16/kai-jones-wants-more-playing-time-texas-longhorns/ |accessdate=January 15, 2020 |work=Bahamas Tribune |date=December 16, 2019}} As a freshman, Jones averaged 3.6 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Davis |first1=Brian |title=Big 12 tournament men’s preview: No. 4 seed Texas vs. No. 5 seed Texas Tech |url=https://www.hookem.com/2020/03/11/big-12-tournament-mens-preview-no-4-seed-texas-vs-no-5-seed-texas-tech/ |accessdate=April 10, 2020 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=March 11, 2020}} On January 26, 2021, he registered his first [[double-double]], with 15 points and 10 rebounds in an 80–79 loss to [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite web |last1=Dorsett |first1=Renaldo |title=Kai Jones posts his first double double in NCAA |url=http://www.tribune242.com/news/2021/jan/28/kai-jones-posts-his-first-double-double-ncaa/ |website=The Tribune |access-date=July 22, 2021 |date=January 28, 2021}} Jones was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Sixth Man of the Year and to the All-Big 12 honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Wallace |first1=Roger |title=Longhorns’ Kai Jones named Big 12 Sixth Man of the Year |url=https://www.kxan.com/sports/longhorns-kai-jones-named-big-12-sixth-man-of-the-year/ |website=[[KXAN-TV]] |access-date=July 22, 2021 |date=March 8, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 8.8 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. On March 24, 2021, Jones declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Madeline |title=Texas Forward Kai Jones Declares for NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/03/24/kai-jones-texas-declares-nba-draft |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 22, 2021 |date=March 24, 2021}} ==National team career== Jones was a member of the Bahamian junior national team at the 2017 [[Centrobasket]] Under-17 Championship in the [[Dominican Republic]]. His team finished seventh place out of eight teams.{{cite web |last1=French |first1=Simba |title=Groups for 2019 Centrobasket U-17 Championships revealed |url=https://thenassauguardian.com/2019/05/04/groups-for-2019-centrobasket-u-17-championships-revealed/ |website=[[The Nassau Guardian]] |accessdate=September 15, 2019 |date=May 4, 2019}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] | '''27''' || '''10''' || 16.7 || .500 || .292 || .636 || 3.2 || .4 || .5 || '''1.1''' || 3.6 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas]] | 26 || 4 || '''22.8''' || '''.580''' || '''.382''' || '''.689''' || '''4.8''' || '''.6''' || '''.8''' || .9 || '''8.8''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 53 || 14 || 19.7 || .553 || .345 || .677 || 4.0 || .5 || .7 || 1.0 || 6.2 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://texassports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/kai-jones/10343 Texas Longhorns bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Jones, Kai}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bahamian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Bahamian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Nassau, Bahamas]]
